title: Fix the triage prompt
scenario: Your support inbox takes 200+ messages a day. A teammate drafted a prompt for the AI assistant that sorts them — it works, but the results are different on every run and cannot be explained to anyone.
task: Rewrite the weak prompt so the sorting is a rulebook: categories, priority criteria, an unclear bucket and a fixed output shape. Then compare with a strong version.
weakPrompt: Sort these customer messages by importance and tell me what to do first.

criteria.label: Explicit categories with boundaries
criteria.hint: Name each category — Billing, Technical, Shipping, Account access — and where its edges lie.

criteria.label: Priority as criteria, not a feeling
criteria.hint: Define what ranks higher: safety, money lost today, blocked work…

criteria.label: A bucket for messages that do not fit
criteria.hint: 'Needs human review' for cases that fit none or several — never a forced guess.

criteria.label: A fixed output shape with a reason per message
criteria.hint: One list per category, one line per message, a five-word reason for its placement.

sampleSolution:
Sort these customer messages into exactly these categories: Billing, Technical, Shipping, Account access, Other. If a message fits more than one category, place it by the most severe issue and note the second category.

Rank the messages within each category by this priority order: (1) safety risks, (2) money lost today — charges, double billing, (3) blocked work, (4) everything else.

If a message does not clearly fit — or fits none — put it under 'Needs human review' instead of guessing.

Output one list per category. For each message: one line with its position and a five-word reason. Use only what the messages say; do not invent details.

Messages:
[paste messages]
hints: What does 'importance' mean to five different people?
Where should an ambiguous message go, so it is not lost?
explanation: The weak prompt hands the model a feeling and hopes for consistency. The rewrite replaces the feeling with a rulebook: named categories with edges, a ranked priority order, an explicit bucket for unclear cases, and an output shape with a five-word reason per message — so any row can be audited at a glance and the hard cases stay visible.
